What the Compiler Explorer link shows, and what it deliberately does not
=======================================================================

Link: https://godbolt.org/z/aYqW8oeWE
Panes: dxc_1_6_2112, dxc_trunk (both `-T vs_6_0 -E VS`),
       fxc_10_0_19041 (`/T vs_5_0 /E VS`).
Full pane text: manual-case-godbolt-verify.txt.

READ THIS BEFORE SEARCHING THE PANES FOR `mPos`
-----------------------------------------------
Every pane in this link contains the literal strings `mPos` and `mColor`, and
in none of them does that mean reflection can retrieve them. This is the one
way to read this link wrong, so it is first.

* The DXC panes contain them because Compiler Explorer appends its own debug
  flags. The panes prove it themselves -- each one ends with

      !48 = !{!"-E", !"VS", !"-T", !"vs_6_0", !"-Zi", !"-Qembed_debug"}

  so `-Zi -Qembed_debug` embeds the entire source text into
  `!dx.source.contents` (which includes this repro's comment header, itself
  quoting the issue) and emits DWARF member metadata:

      !34 = !DIDerivedType(tag: DW_TAG_member, name: "mPos", scope: !32, ...)
      !32 = !DICompositeType(tag: DW_TAG_structure_type, name: "VertexIn", ...)

  That is debug information. `ID3D12ShaderReflection` does not read it, and a
  shipping shader is not normally compiled with it.

* The FXC pane contains them in its listing comment:

      // Initial variable locations:
      //   v0.x <- vin.mPos.x; v0.y <- vin.mPos.y; v0.z <- vin.mPos.z;

  That is FXC's disassembly annotation, not a reflection field either. It is,
  however, the closest thing in either compiler to what the issue asks for,
  which is worth knowing.

The local evidence is not vulnerable to this: `cmd.txt` is `-T vs_6_0 -E VS`
with no debug flags, and manual-case-witnesses.txt walks the reflection API
itself rather than reading disassembly text.

WHAT TO ACTUALLY LOOK AT
------------------------
1. The input signature, in all three panes. DXC prints

       ; Name                 Index   Mask Register SysValue  Format   Used
       ; POSITION                 0   xyz         0     NONE   float   xyz
       ; COLOR                    0   xyz         1     NONE   float   xyz

   and FXC prints the same table under `// Input signature:`. A signature
   element is identified by its semantic. There is no column for the HLSL
   member the semantic came from, in either compiler, because
   D3D12_SIGNATURE_PARAMETER_DESC has no such field.

2. The contrast with the constant buffer, in all three panes. The buffer
   definitions block names HLSL members:

       //       float3 cbAlpha;                // Offset:    0

   Both compilers can name a struct's members -- when the struct is a constant
   buffer. `CbStruct` in this repro exists only to make that contrast visible
   in the same compilation; it is not part of the reported problem.

3. The metadata behind that contrast, in the DXC panes. `!dx.typeAnnotations`
   is the reflection type table, and it has an entry for the cbuffer struct:

       !55 = !{i32 0, %struct.CbStruct undef, !56, %Params undef, !59}
       !57 = !{i32 6, !"cbAlpha", i32 3, i32 0, i32 7, i32 9}

   (tag 6 is kDxilFieldAnnotationFieldNameTag). There is no corresponding
   entry for the entry point's parameter struct. Searching either DXC pane for
   `%struct.VertexIn` finds nothing at all: the type does not survive into the
   module, so there is nothing for reflection to annotate. The input signature
   is instead metadata keyed by semantic string:

       !68 = !{i32 0, !"POSITION", i8 9, i8 0, !69, i8 0, i32 1, i8 3, ...}

   Note that this holds even in these panes, which were compiled with `-Zi`
   and therefore keep reflection metadata in the module -- the annotation is
   not being stripped, it is never created.

WHY FXC IS IN THE LINK
----------------------
The question is whether this is a DXC gap or the D3D reflection model. FXC is
the reference implementation of that model, and
tools/clang/unittests/HLSL/DxilContainerTest.cpp compiles the same shader with
d3dcompiler.lib and asserts DXC's reflection matches it field by field. The
FXC pane shows FXC naming signature elements by semantic and cbuffer fields by
identifier, exactly as DXC does. So the answer the issue got is a property of
the API, not a DXC-specific omission -- which is why the suggested action is a
feature request against the reflection surface rather than a bug report.

Clang is deliberately absent: hlsl_clang_trunk cannot lower vertex-stage
signature I/O, so a pane would show a failure that has nothing to do with this
issue.
